what_the_class_is: The 3D chorus as a whole: a chorus voice an output, the balance of dry against wet, then the level and tone stages.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at 32 kHz with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A chorus is a delay line whose read address a modulator moves, summed with the dry path; the per-sample cost is one interpolated read a voice and a multiply-accumulate to mix it, so six voices cost six reads and nothing else new.

The modulator is a phase accumulator read through a short shape, and a triangle is the cheapest shape: a folded ramp needs no table. Several voices off one accumulator are that accumulator read at several offsets.

A chorus built after a two-line analogue design feeds each output both lines, one of them inverted, so that the delayed copies cancel in a mono sum; a digital copy of that design costs one more multiply-accumulate an output.
Rates, times and levels are tables indexed by the byte, as the classes that read them closed on; a whole-type model borrows those tables rather than fitting its own.
era.would_be_wrong_if: A reading of the delay's excursion placed the unit's settings outside what either shape predicts by more than the reading's own floor at settings nothing here was built on, or a byte this family reads through a shared table returned values that table does not hold.

candidates.reading: The modulator is a triangle spanning the depth above the pre-delay, and the depth byte is worth the stereo chorus's pitch excursion read as a delay under that shape. The modulator's shape (triangle) and how the outputs' modulators stand: one modulator for both.
candidates.predicts: The same wet signal on both outputs, so no width from the chorus itself. Its delay moves at one rate from end to end, so its pitch holds two values a cycle and jumps between them.

candidates.reading: The modulator is a raised sine spanning the depth above the pre-delay, and the depth byte is worth the stereo chorus's pitch excursion read as a delay under that shape. The modulator's shape (raised sine) and how the outputs' modulators stand: one modulator for both.
candidates.predicts: The same wet signal on both outputs, so no width from the chorus itself. Its delay lingers at the ends of the sweep and passes the middle quickly, and at every depth its excursion is 0.64 of the triangle's.

candidates.predicts: Outputs whose delays move in opposite directions, so a wet path that differs between the sides by the modulator's whole swing. Its delay moves at one rate from end to end, so its pitch holds two values a cycle and jumps between them.
